sheet-title.purpose: Checkpoint file and Assistant in the header strip; the widest tracking in the system.

state-title.purpose: Empty, error and no-folder card headings, on both sheets.

station-title.purpose: Checkpoint names on the sheet; the tightest tracking, ellipsized on a character budget, never wrapped.

prose.purpose: What a sheet carries: the state card's body and the assistant transcript's messages, including the awaiting slot — the system's only sentence-case running text, and the only text allowed to wrap.

code.purpose: The code block's body and its target path — the editor's own monospace at 11px, the one tier that keeps its own case. Never chrome, never prose.

micro-tag.purpose: The type · time · active line under each station name, the message row's role · time tag and the code block's TARGET label; provenance lives here.

micro-title.purpose: The carried-from row's checkpoint title — station weight at the micro scale, ellipsized to one line.

sheet-meta.purpose: Footer legend, rendition note, the assistant's carried-from row and the composer hint; the header's record count is the same size one step wider (0.16em) and the assistant header's model id the same size tighter and uncased (0.06em).

sheet-count.purpose: The map header's N records — 8.5px at 0.16em, the widest of the small print.

sheet-ident.purpose: The assistant header's model id — 8.5px at 0.06em with its case kept; the one uncased string in the chrome.

ring-number.purpose: Control order printed beside each control ring, counting the course from the origin to the active checkpoint.

shadows.name: floating-platform-chrome
shadows.purpose: Context menu only — platform chrome floating over the flat sheet. Neither sheet has a shadow vocabulary.

motion.name: evograph-invert
motion.purpose: Whole-sheet invert flash when the active checkpoint changes — both the map and the assistant; dropped under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: hard-cut-states
motion.purpose: Hover, selection, focus, disabled and menu changes are instant; neither stylesheet declares a transition property.

components.name: Checkpoint Station — On Course
components.description: The atom of the sheet: a numbered control ring with the station name 22px right of the control centre and the type · time micro-tag 15px below it, on a 56px hit row. The label sits on a ground-coloured knockout plate (rx=2, drawn first in the station group: 16px right of the lane centre, 36px tall, text estimate plus 12px of air) so no line is ever drawn across a name.

narrative.overview:
The checkpoint file is printed, not rendered. The panel is one sheet in three strips — a header that names the file, its record count and its rendition; a routed canvas; a footer legend — and everything on it obeys two printed languages at once: transit wayfinding (routes, stations, a legend, time read downward) and an orienteering course map (numbered controls, a course thread, control descriptions set in tiny caps). The ground is paper in the light theme and night in the dark theme, and the sheet names which it is: day map or night race. The theme chooses the rendition; it never changes the artifact. A second sheet now prints from the same press: the assistant panel, a correspondence log in the identical three strips — header, transcript, composer — capped to a reading measure instead of to a drawing, where chrome stays caps and what it carries sets in sentence case or the editor's monospace.

Two drawings share the page. The first is the network: an ink trunk routed at true 45° elbows, alternate branches peeling right in pale blue, stations marked either as numbered control rings (on the course) or as a plain 22px ink bar (everything off it). The second is the course laid over it: one violet thread through the rings that the developer actually rode, dashed violet ghosts where an abandoned leg still hangs, and a tinted flood across the active control's row. The signature move is that the course redraws whole on every switch and the sheet inverts for 170ms — the ride is visible as one printed act, not a sequence of component updates.

Density is instrument-like. Type stays between 8.5px and 12px, uppercase almost everywhere, with hierarchy carried by weight, tracking and color rather than size. Three hairlines and one tinted band do all the layering, and there is exactly one shadow in the system — on a floating menu that is not part of the sheet. It refuses the category's dot-and-hairline git graph: routes here are 7px, turns are 45°, and every checkpoint holds a place on a course rather than a row in a list.
keyCharacteristics: A sheet in three strips: header (title, record count, rendition note), routed canvas, footer legend — one 1px rule each side of the canvas.
Transit geometry: a 76px lane step, an 84px row pitch, true 45° elbows, 7px routed trunks with a 4.5px violet thread riding on top.
Orienteering vocabulary: numbered control rings, ghost dashes for abandoned legs, a flood on the active control, a 22px tick for everything off the course.
Two renditions of one identity: day map and night race. Ground, ink, dim and rule follow the theme; the four accents keep their identity and only retune for contrast.
One bundled condensed signage face, 8.5–12px, uppercase chrome — hierarchy by weight, tracking and color — plus one borrowed instrument: the editor's monospace for code content, and nothing else.

Two sheets, one base: the checkpoint map (capped to its drawing) and the assistant log (capped to a 360px reading measure) share one base stylesheet — the signage face, the four rendition token sets, the header strip, the state card, the state action and the single 170ms invert.
Depth without shadows: hairlines, a tinted band, punched rings, and layer order.
Motion is a single event: a 170ms invert flash when the active checkpoint changes. Every other state change is hard-cut — there is not one `transition` in the stylesheets.

rules.name: The Ridden Path Rule
rules.body: Violet is the record of the ride. The course thread, the control rings, their numbers, the ghost dashes, the flood and the hover wash are violet because the developer has been there; a violet mark that records nothing is a lie about the history.

rules.name: The Branch Borrows Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue belongs to branch lines and their legend key — nowhere else. A branch never marks selection, action, or the active checkpoint; the trunk stays ink so that "the main line" and "a line taken" are told apart by colour and not only by position.

rules.name: The Provenance Stays In The Tag Rule
rules.body: Olive ("AI prompt") and amber ("AI applied") exist for two strings at 8.5px caps — the station micro-tag and the carried-from row's type tag. Origin and manual records stay faded ink. A checkpoint's type never colours its line, its ring, or its row — provenance is a label on a station, never a route.

rules.name: The Twelve-Pixel Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the sheet is larger than 12px. Hierarchy is carried by weight, caps, tracking and colour — never by a size jump. A surface that needs a 20px heading is not this sheet.

rules.name: The One Lowercase Sentence Rule
rules.body: Chrome stays caps: everything a sheet says about itself — titles, tags, labels, hints, legends — is uppercase. What a sheet carries is content, and content sets in sentence case: the state card's body copy and the assistant transcript's messages are the prose tier — one voice, the only tier with a declared line-height, and the only text allowed to wrap. Code content is neither caps nor sentence case: it keeps its own case in the monospace.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Exactly two voices ship, plus one borrowed instrument: the bundled condensed signage face for the sheet; the platform's own UI face for VS Code chrome (the context menu) and for the controls that are the platform's; and the editor's own monospace for code content only. No system display face, no icon font, no monospace anywhere else.

rules.name: The Read-Down Rule
rules.body: Time runs down and branch depth runs right — the footer says it: read down = time. Time is never laid horizontally and the sheet is never rotated.

rules.name: The Forty-Five Rule
rules.body: Every route change of direction is a true 45° elbow: vertical, then a diagonal exactly as long as the lane offset, then vertical again. No curves, no beziers, no arcs anywhere in the routing.

rules.name: The Sheet Width Rule
rules.body: The drawing sets the sheet's width and the header and footer cap to it. Chrome never outruns the drawing, and the drawing never compresses below 300px. Where a sheet's content is prose rather than a drawing, the printed measure sets the cap instead (The Printed Measure Rule).

rules.name: The Printed Measure Rule
rules.body: A sheet that carries sustained prose prints to a measure, not to the panel: the assistant caps its header, transcript and composer at 360px — a nominal 74-character measure at 11.5px condensed, 72 measured at the cap — and where the panel is wider the ground continues past it, exactly as it does under the map. A sheet whose content is a drawing caps to the drawing instead.

rules.name: The Knockout Plate Rule
rules.body: A station's label is printed on a plate, not laid over the map: the name and micro-tag sit on a ground-coloured block drawn first in the station group, so the trunk, the branch lines, the ghost dashes and the course thread stop at the block and resume past it — while the row's own flood and hover washes still tint it. The sheet never asks the reader to choose between the line and the word: a line is never drawn across a name.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: The sheet is flat at rest and in every state. Layering is done with 1px rules, one tinted band and draw order; the moment a sheet element needs a shadow to be legible, the hierarchy has failed, not the shadow budget.

rules.name: The Two-Pixel Rule
rules.body: 2px is the entire radius budget for rectangles in this system — the flooded row, its focus ring and the label plate. Everything else that is rectangular is square; anything that is round is a control.

rules.name: The Punched Control Rule
rules.body: A control ring is filled with the ground, not left transparent: the course thread runs behind the control, so each ring reads as a hole punched in the route. Circles are reserved for on-course checkpoints, and only on-course checkpoints carry numbers.

rules.name: The Dash Means Ghost Rule
rules.body: Dashes carry one meaning wherever they appear: nothing is there yet — a leg that was never ridden (9/7 dash), a sheet with no records (the card's dashed border), a reply that has not arrived (the awaiting slot). Never decorative.

dos: Do keep the layer order: trunk and branches, then ghost legs, then the course thread, then stations.
Do draw the course thread whole — one polyline through every control from origin to the active checkpoint on every render. Never animate it segment by segment.
Do keep the flood at 14% and the hover wash at 7% in the day rendition, so an aimed row never reads as the current row.

Do keep provenance in the type tag: olive for "AI prompt", amber for "AI applied", faded ink for origin and manual — in the station micro-tag and the carried-from row. A type never colours a line, a ring or a row.

Do keep everything a sheet says about itself uppercase, in the bundled condensed face, between 8.5px and 12px; keep what a sheet carries in the prose tier, and keep code content in the editor's monospace, nowhere else.
Do cap the assistant at the 360px measure — header, transcript and composer ending on one right edge — and let the ground continue past it, exactly as it does under the map.
Do keep every action the same state action (Send, Apply, Retry, Set API key), and let the row be the button where the row already carries the action.
Do let the theme choose the rendition and the header name it; retune ground, ink, dim and rule and all four accents together, never one alone.
Do keep the 2px radii to the flooded band, its focus ring and the label plate, keep off-course records as a 22px tick, and keep every route turn at 45°.
Do keep the hit row at least 56px tall and 160px wide, with a visible focus ring on :focus-visible.
donts: Don't use blue for anything but branch lines and their legend key — not for selection, not for links, not for the active checkpoint.
Don't use olive or amber outside the provenance type tag — the station micro-tag and the carried-from row.
Don't number off-course records: numbered rings belong to the course (origin down to the active checkpoint), everything else is a tick.
Don't add radii beyond 2px, shadows on the sheet, gradients or translucency.

Don't set type above 12px on the sheet, or add a face to it: the three voices are settled — the bundled signage face, the platform's own UI face for the platform's chrome and its controls, and the editor's monospace for code content only. No system display face, no icon font, no monospace anywhere else.
Don't restyle platform chrome: the context menu keeps the platform UI face and its native menu tokens.
Don't give the transcript a role colour, a bubble or an avatar: roles are told apart by the tag word alone.
Don't stretch a prose sheet to the panel: chrome never outruns the measure, exactly as it never outruns the drawing.
Don't route a line with curves, arcs or any diagonal other than 45°.
Don't introduce a fourth accent to mean "selected": selection is flood + ring weight + the deep-violet tag, not a new hue.
Don't lay time horizontally or rotate the sheet.
